title: Latest Time You Can Obtain After Replacing Characters
statement:
The string `s` has the shape `"HH:MM"` and describes a time on a 12-hour clock, but some of its digits (possibly none) are hidden and shown as `'?'`. A time counts as valid when `HH` is from `00` to `11` and `MM` is from `00` to `59`, so the earliest valid time is `"00:00"` and the latest is `"11:59"`.

Put a digit in place of every `'?'` so that the result is a valid time, choosing the latest valid time you can make, and return that string. The input always allows at least one valid time.
constraints: Every character of s other than s[2] is a digit or '?'
At least one time from "00:00" to "11:59" can be formed by replacing the '?' characters
notes:
## Intuition

A 12-hour clock has only 12 × 60 = 720 possible times. Instead of reasoning about each `'?'` separately, walk through those times from the latest (`11:59`) to the earliest (`00:00`) and stop at the first one that agrees with `s` everywhere a digit is shown. Because the walk goes from latest to earliest, the first fit is the answer.

## Approach

1. Loop `hour` from 11 down to 0, and inside it `minute` from 59 down to 0.
2. Build the candidate `time` as `"HH:MM"`, padding each part to two digits.
3. Compare it with `s` position by position: a `'?'` accepts any digit, but a shown character must be equal. Set `matches` to false on the first conflict.
4. Return the first `time` that still matches. The guarantee means one always exists.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "1?:?4"`. The first candidate is `"11:59"`: positions 0 to 3 fit, but `s[4] = '4'` differs from `'9'`. The same happens for `"11:58"` through `"11:55"`. At `"11:54"`, `'1'` matches `'1'`, both `'?'` accept their digits, `':'` matches and `'4'` matches `'4'`, so the function returns `"11:54"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): at most 720 candidates, each compared in 5 steps.
- Space: O(1): only the current candidate string is kept.

## Pitfalls

- Hours stop at `11`, not `12` or `23`: `"?2:00"` must become `"02:00"`, not `"12:00"`.
- Pad single-digit hours and minutes with a leading zero, or the positions will not line up with `s`.
- A greedy fill must look at the neighbouring digit: the first hour digit can be `1` only when the second is `'?'`, `0` or `1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hour` | candidate hour, from 11 down to 0 |
| `minute` | candidate minute, from 59 down to 0 |
| `time` | the candidate written as `"HH:MM"` |
| `matches` | whether every shown character of `s` agrees with `time` |
| `i` | position being compared |

narration.2: Try hours from the latest, 11, down to 0.
narration.3: For each hour, try minutes from 59 down to 0, so candidates come latest first.
narration.4: Write the candidate as "HH:MM", padding each part to two digits so positions line up with s.
narration.5: Assume the candidate fits until a conflict appears.
narration.6: Compare all five positions of s with the candidate.
narration.7: A shown character that differs from the candidate rules it out; a '?' accepts anything.
narration.8: Record the conflict and stop comparing this candidate.
narration.12: Every shown character agreed with this candidate.
narration.13: It is the latest time that fits, because candidates were tried latest first.
narration.17: Unreachable for valid input, since some time always fits.
